content: In the United States, if you experience side effects, contact your doctor for medical advice. Similarly, in Canada, consult your doctor for guidance regarding side effects. Precautions: Before using granisetron, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other issues. Granisetron may be affected by sunlight or increase the sensitivity of the application site to sunlight. While wearing the patch, keep it covered (e.g. Avoid tanning booths. After removing the patch, keep the application site covered for an additional 10 days. If you are scheduled for an MRI, inform the testing personnel that you are using this patch, as some patches may contain metals that can cause serious burns during an MRI. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if clearly necessary. It is unknown whether this medication passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use (including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. The risk of serotonin syndrome or toxicity increases if you are also taking other drugs that elevate serotonin levels. Examples include street drugs like MDMA (ecstasy), St. John’s wort, and certain antidepressants (e.g., SSRIs like fluoxetine or paroxetine, and SNRIs like duloxetine or venlafaxine). Overdose: If the patch is chewed or swallowed, it may be harmful. In the event of an overdose, remove the patch if possible. For severe symptoms such as fainting or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose or fail to use the patch at the correct time before your scheduled chemotherapy appointment, inform your doctor. Storage: Store the patch at room temperature, away from heat. Do not open the pouch until you are ready to use the patch. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This summary does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Uses: This medication is used to prevent nausea and vomiting caused by cancer drug treatment (chemotherapy). How to Use: Read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist before starting this medication and each time you get a refill. Follow all instructions for proper application and use of the patch. Do not cut the patch into smaller sizes or use it if it appears broken, cut, or damaged. Apply the patch to the skin as directed by your doctor, usually 1 to 2 days (24 to 48 hours) before your chemotherapy treatment. Do not open the sealed pouch until you are ready to use the patch. Remove the patch from the protective liner and apply it to a clean, dry area on the outer part of your upper arm. Avoid applying the patch to recently shaved, oily, red, irritated, or broken skin, or areas where you have applied skin products like creams or lotions. You can bathe and shower with the patch on. Wash your hands with soap and water after each application. Wear the patch during your chemotherapy treatment and for at least 24 hours after completing treatment. Do not wear the patch for more than 7 consecutive days. If the patch does not stick well, use medical tape or surgical bandages to secure the edges. When removing the patch, peel it off gently, fold it in half with the sticky sides together, and discard it in the trash, away from children and pets. Do not reuse the patch. Wash the application site and your hands with soap and water. Mild redness at the application site may occur but should resolve within 3 days. Use this medication exactly as directed to achieve the best results. Do not use more medication than prescribed. Side Effects: Constipation may occur. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. This medication may increase serotonin levels and, in rare cases, cause a serious condition called serotonin syndrome or toxicity. The risk increases if you are also taking other drugs that elevate serotonin levels. Inform your doctor or pharmacist of all the medications you are taking. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance regarding side effects.
